title: Separated universal homeomorphisms of algebraic spaces are affine
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $X,Y$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $r:X\to Y$ be an $S$-morphism. Suppose that $r$ is separated, meaning its diagonal $X\to X\times_YX$ is a closed immersion, and that $r$ is a universal homeomorphism, meaning that $|X\times_YT|\to|T|$ is a homeomorphism for every algebraic space $T\to Y$. A closed immersion is tested on etale scheme charts and is given by quotienting by a quasi-coherent ideal. Then $r$ is representable by schemes and integral. More explicitly, for every scheme $T\to Y$, $X\times_YT$ is a scheme and its map to $T$ is affine: the inverse image of an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq T$ is $\operatorname{Spec}B$ for an $A$-algebra $B$ integral over $A$, meaning that every element of $B$ satisfies a monic polynomial over $A$.

source.place: Rydh, Submersions and effective descent of etale morphisms, Corollary (5.22), printed pp.24--25, and Appendix B opening paragraph, printed p.38. Read author PDF online at https://davidrydh.se/papers/submersion20100305.pdf; local copy WANTED. The paper assumes quasi-separated spaces globally. For the stated arbitrary-space form one works etale locally over affine charts of Y: the source is quasi-compact by universal closedness and separated over the affine chart, hence quasi-separated, so Corollary (5.22) applies there and representability/integrality descend etale locally.

proof.text: Fix any scheme $T\to Y$ and put $Z=X\times_YT$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. For every $C\to T$, $Z\times_TC=X\times_YC$ by the fibre-product universal property; thus $Z\to T$ is a universal homeomorphism by the given hypothesis. It is separated by [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition]. We may first take $T$ affine; the last step will handle arbitrary $T$. The homeomorphism $|Z|\simeq|T|$ makes $|Z|$ quasi-compact since affine schemes are quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Apply [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas] to choose an affine scheme $U'$ and a representable surjective etale map $u':U'\to Z$.

source.place: Tags 03H6 (affine atlas for a quasi-compact space) and 03KL (base change of separatedness); Rydh Corollary (5.22), choosing the presentation after affine base change.

proof.text: The affine schemes $T$ and $U'$ are absolutely separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated] and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. The scheme diagonal of $T$ is a closed immersion, and every scheme pullback of it remains a closed immersion [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]; hence it is a closed immersion also under the scheme-test definition for spaces. Composing $Z\to T$ with $T\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ gives absolute separatedness of $Z$ [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition]. Its absolute diagonal is therefore a closed immersion, hence proper and quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-space-closed-subspace-proper]. Thus $Z$ is quasi-separated. Finally, the absolutely separated scheme $U'$ has separated etale chart $u':U'\to Z$ by [lem-a1-separated-etale-chart]. These verify all quasi-separated-space and separated-object hypotheses of the next step.

source.place: Tags 04ZH (separated over separated), 04XZ (closed immersions proper), and spaces-properties 03FZ (separated scheme charts). Rydh printed p.4 convention, made explicit.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-homeomorphism-separated-etale-equivalence] to $Z\to T$ and its separated etale object $U'\to Z$. It supplies a quasi-separated algebraic space $U$, a separated chartwise etale map $u:U\to T$, and an isomorphism $U\times_TZ\simeq U'$ over $Z$. Since $T$ is a scheme, [lem-a1-separated-etale-space-scheme] makes $U$ a scheme and $u$ an etale scheme morphism. By [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], the surjective atlas $U'\to Z$ is surjective on point spaces. Together with the homeomorphism $|Z|\simeq|T|$, its composite $U'\to Z\to T$ is surjective on point spaces. It factors through $u$, so $|u|$ is surjective; thus $u$ is a surjective etale scheme morphism. No representability of a general etale space over $T$ was assumed before applying the separated-etale scheme criterion.

source.place: Corollary (5.22), printed pp.24-25, using Theorem (5.21); the intermediate separated-etale object is represented using Stacks 03XX and 03XU.

proof.text: The projection $U'=Z\times_TU\to U$ is a universal homeomorphism: after every further scheme base change its point map is one of the homeomorphisms in the hypothesis on $r$. Both $U'$ and $U$ are now schemes. Hence [lem-trf-universally-homeomorph-integral] makes this projection integral, and therefore affine by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Apply [lem-sfb-space-affine-locality] to the surjective etale scheme morphism $U\to T$. It follows that $Z\to T$ is affine. In particular $Z$ is a scheme (indeed affine since $T$ is affine). Applying [lem-trf-universally-homeomorph-integral] again, now to the scheme morphism $Z\to T$, shows that it is integral.

source.place: Corollary (5.22), printed p.25, representable universal homeomorphism and etale descent of affineness; Stacks 04DF and 03WG.

proof.text: Let $T\to Y$ be any scheme test and write $Z_T=X\times_YT$. For every affine open $V\subseteq T$, step 4 gives an affine scheme $Z_V=X\times_YV$. If $W\subseteq V$ is another affine open, fibre-product associativity identifies $Z_W$ with the open subscheme $Z_V\times_VW$; these restriction maps have identity and composition laws by their projections. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-relative-glueing-affine-opens] gives a scheme $P\to T$ with these restrictions. It represents $Z_T$: over any test scheme $C\to T$, the opens $C\times_TV$ cover $C$; maps into $P$ and sections of $Z_T$ both glue uniquely from these opens, and their local identifications are precisely the same $Z_V$. The local comparisons and their inverses therefore glue to mutually inverse natural transformations. Here the sheaf property is part of [def-trf-algebraic-space], and maps into schemes glue by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. Now $P\to T$ has affine inverse image over every affine open, so [pqf-lem-affine-local-target] makes it affine. The base-change identity in step 1 makes it a universal homeomorphism; [lem-trf-universally-homeomorph-integral] makes it integral. Finally [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] gives the required monic-polynomial description of every $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$. All scheme tests are therefore represented and integral.
